title: Purpose-dependent reduced-state sufficiency before LARE closure dynamics
research_question: Which conservative vertical state information must be retained for declared hydrological purposes before any LARE flux closure is fitted or evaluated?

distinction.alternative_numerical_solver: targets essentially the same Richards solution and therefore remains subject to strict numerical and hydrological equivalence
distinction.reduced_hydrological_model: may admit bounded departures from Richards when they remain inside a preregistered purpose-dependent hydrological acceptance envelope

state_first_rule: Reduced-state sufficiency is adjudicated before LARE, EQ-LARE, learned, fitted, or other propagation dynamics are introduced.

retrospective_pilot_evidence.interpretation_firewall: Numerical state separation in these short near-equilibrium libraries is not hydrological sufficiency and does not authorize a LARE solver.

RS1_GW.purpose: groundwater recharge, capillary rise, storage and flux-reversal fidelity

RS1_HUPSEL.purpose: realistic agricultural water-balance, ET, drainage and root-zone state fidelity
RS1_HUPSEL.observation_rule: Add profile observation only. Do not change physics, solver, timestep, retry, tolerance, forcing, process composition or accepted application intervals.

required_regimes: dry profile plus intense rainfall pulse

candidate_representation_policy.conservative_state: layer water storage W_i = integral(theta dz)

purpose_dependent_gate.collision_definition: Two accepted full-order states are close in the candidate reduced coordinate but distinguishable in full state under an independently frozen numerical floor.
purpose_dependent_gate.failure_definition: A collision becomes a reduced-state failure only when identical future forcing causes a difference in a preregistered purpose output larger than that purpose's acceptance envelope.

comparators_after_state_survival: coarse Richards on exactly the same candidate partitions
equilibrium-subtracted LARE if standard LARE fails hydrostatic preservation
